paragraphs: Art. 1. (1) Documents and other papers are legalised and certified in Bulgaria by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and abroad by the diplomatic and consular missions of Bulgaria.

(2) Certification under the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents is made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Justice, the National Centre for Information and Documentation and the regional administrations, as the authorities competent to issue the certificate under Art. 3(1) of that Convention.
Art. 6. Documents and other papers signed by private persons are legalised only if the signatures are notarially certified and the notary's signature is certified by the Ministry of Justice.
Art. 7. After legalisation by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the document must be certified by the diplomatic or consular mission of the country for which it is intended.

17а.title: Apostille
paragraphs: Art. 17a. (1) Certification under the Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation is made by issuing the "apostille" certificate under Art. 3(1) of the Convention. It certifies the authenticity of the signature, the capacity in which the signatory acted and, where needed, the identity of the seal or stamp on the document.
(2) The authorities competent in Bulgaria are:

1. the Ministry of Justice – for documents issued by an authority or official connected with the courts, including documents of a prosecutor, a court clerk or a process server, notarial acts, and official certifications such as registrations or certifications of a date or a signature on a private document;
2. the National Centre for Information and Documentation – for educational documents issued by universities, schools and vocational training institutions and by the Ministry of Education and Science;
3. the regional administrations – for documents issued by mayors and municipal administrations;
4. the Ministry of Foreign Affairs – for all other administrative documents with the certification under Art. 3 and 4.
(3) The Ministry of Justice provides the service within 2 working days.

(4) The National Centre provides it within three working days for documents not in the public registers of the Ministry of Education, and within eight working hours, electronically, for documents in those registers.
(5) The authorities under para. 2, items 3 and 4 provide it within eight working hours, or up to two working days when objective circumstances require.

21а.title: Translator's signature
paragraphs: Art. 21a. (1) For a foreign document translated into Bulgarian in Bulgaria under these Regulations and intended for use in Bulgaria, the translator's signature on the translation must be notarially certified in Bulgaria. When the signature is certified, the translator presents to the notary the document under Art. 18(2).

(2) For a Bulgarian document translated into a foreign language in Bulgaria and intended for use abroad, the translator's signature is certified by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, if the country of use requires or accepts this.
